bookInfo.name: Old History of the Five Dynasties
bookInfo.author: Xue Juzheng et al.

title.zh: 卷七十二 唐書48: 列傳24 張承業 張居翰 馬紹宏 孟漢瓊
title.en: Volume 72 Book of Later Tang 48: Biographies 24 - Zhang Chengye, Zhang Juhan, Ma Shaohong, Meng Hangqiong
title.raw: 卷七十二 唐書48: 列傳24 張承業 張居翰 馬紹宏 孟漢瓊 Volume 72 Book of Later Tang 48: Biographies 24 - Zhang Chengye, Zhang Juhan, Ma Shaohong, Meng Hangqiong

sentences.zh: 張承業，字繼元，本姓康，同州人。

translations.literal: Zhang Chengye, styled Jiyuan, was originally of the Kang clan and a native of Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chengye, whose style was Jiyuan, came from the Kang clan of Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 咸通中，內常侍張泰畜為假子。

translations.literal: During the Xiantong era, Inner Attendant Zhang Tai took him as a foster son.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiantong period Inner Attendant Zhang Tai adopted him.

sentences.zh: 光啟中，主郃陽軍事，賜紫，入為內供奉。

translations.literal: During Guangqi he oversaw military affairs at Heyang, was granted purple robes, and entered service as an inner palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Under Guangqi he directed Heyang's military affairs, received the purple robe, and became an inner palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 武皇之討王行瑜，承業累奉使渭北，因留監武皇軍事，賊平，改酒坊使。

translations.literal: When Wuhuang campaigned against Wang Xingyu, Chengye repeatedly went on missions north of the Wei River, then stayed to oversee Wuhuang's army; after the rebels were pacified he was made wine-works commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: During Wuhuang's campaign against Wang Xingyu, Chengye went repeatedly to the Wei north, remained to supervise the army, and after victory was made commissioner of the wine works.

sentences.zh: 三年，昭宗將幸太原，以承業與武皇善，用除為河東監軍，密令迎駕。

translations.literal: In the third year, when Zhaozong was about to visit Taiyuan, because Chengye was on good terms with Wuhuang he was appointed Hedong army inspector with secret orders to welcome the imperial procession.
translations.idiomatic: In year three, as Zhaozong prepared to visit Taiyuan, Chengye's friendship with Wuhuang won him appointment as Hedong army inspector with orders to welcome the throne in secret.

sentences.zh: 既而昭宗幸華州，就加左監門衛將軍。

translations.literal: Soon after, Zhaozong went to Hua Prefecture and Chengye was further made Left Gate Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozong then moved to Hua Prefecture, and Chengye received an additional appointment as Left Gate Guard General.

sentences.zh: 駕在鳳翔，承業屢請出師晉、絳，以為岐人掎角。

translations.literal: While the imperial procession was at Fengxiang, Chengye repeatedly asked to march out from Jin and Jiang to pinch the Qi forces in concert.
translations.idiomatic: With the court at Fengxiang, Chengye urged again and again that armies from Jin and Jiang strike so the Qi could be caught between two fires.

sentences.zh: 崔魏公之誅宦官也，武皇偽戮罪人首級以奉詔，匿承業於斛律寺，昭宗遇弑，乃復請為監軍。

translations.literal: When Chancellor Cui executed the eunuchs, Wuhuang falsely displayed criminals' heads to obey the edict and hid Chengye at Hulu Temple; after Zhaozong was murdered he again requested Chengye as army inspector.
translations.idiomatic: When Chancellor Cui purged the eunuchs, Wuhuang sent false heads to satisfy the edict and hid Chengye at Hulu Temple; after Zhaozong's murder he again asked for him as army inspector.

sentences.zh: 夾城之役，遣承業求援於鳳翔。

translations.literal: During the Jiacheng campaign he was sent to Fengxiang to seek aid.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiacheng affair Chengye was dispatched to Fengxiang for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 時河中阻絕，自離石渡河，春冰方泮，淩澌奔蹙，艤舟不得渡，因禱河神。

translations.literal: The route through Hezhong was cut off; crossing the Yellow River from Lishi, spring ice was just breaking up, floes surged and pressed in, and the boat could not moor to cross, so he prayed to the river god.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhong was blocked; he crossed from Lishi as the spring thaw ran, ice raced downstream, and his boat could not land—so he prayed to the river god.

sentences.zh: 是夜，夢神人謂曰：「子但渡，流冰無患。

translations.literal: That night he dreamed a divine man saying, "Just cross—the drifting ice will do no harm."
translations.idiomatic: That night he dreamed a spirit telling him, "Cross at once; the drifting ice will not harm you."

sentences.zh: 」既寤，津吏報曰：「河冰合矣。

translations.literal: " When he awoke, the ferry officer reported, "The river ice has frozen solid."
translations.idiomatic: When he woke, the ferryman said, "The river has frozen over."

sentences.zh: 」淩晨，躡冰而濟，旋踵冰解。

translations.literal: " At dawn he trod the ice to cross; the moment he reached the far bank the ice broke up.
translations.idiomatic: At first light he crossed on the ice; as soon as he was ashore it melted away.

sentences.zh: 使還，武皇病篤，啟手之夕，召承業屬之曰：「吾兒孤弱，群臣縱橫，後事公善籌之。

translations.literal: On his return Wuhuang was gravely ill; on the night he opened his hand to die he summoned Chengye and entrusted him, saying, "My son is young and weak, the ministers run wild—plan what follows well."
translations.idiomatic: Returning, he found Wuhuang dying; on the night of the dying gesture Wuhuang called Chengye and said, "My boy is alone and the court is unruly—you must guide what comes next."

sentences.zh: 」承業奉遺顧，爰立嗣王，平內難，策略居多。

translations.literal: " Chengye carried out the dying charge, then established the heir, quelled internal strife, and his strategy counted for much.
translations.idiomatic: Chengye honored that charge, set up the heir, settled the civil turmoil, and his counsel weighed heavily in it all.

sentences.zh: 既終易月之制，即請出師救潞，破賊夾城。

translations.literal: After the mourning months ended he at once asked to march out to relieve Lu and broke the rebels at Jiacheng.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he urged a relief march to Lu and smashed the Jiacheng rebels.

sentences.zh: 莊宗深感其意，兄事之，親幸承業私第，升堂拜母，賜遺優厚。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong was deeply moved and treated him as an elder brother, personally visiting Chengye's private residence, ascending the hall to bow to his mother, with lavish gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong cherished him, treated him like an elder brother, visited his home, bowed to his mother in the hall, and heaped gifts upon him.

sentences.zh: 時莊宗初行墨製，凡除拜之命，皆成於盧汝弼之手。

translations.literal: At that time Zhuangzong had just begun issuing orders in his own hand; every appointment and promotion was drafted by Lu Rubi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong had only begun to issue his own writs; Lu Rubi drafted every appointment.

sentences.zh: 汝弼既自為戶部侍郎，乃請與承業改官及開國邑，承業拒而不受。

translations.literal: Rubi had made himself Minister of Revenue and then asked to change Chengye's office and enfeoffment; Chengye refused and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Rubi, now Minister of Revenue, offered to change Chengye's title and fief; Chengye declined.

sentences.zh: 其後，但稱本朝舊官而已。

translations.literal: Thereafter he used only his former Tang titles.
translations.idiomatic: After that he kept only his old Tang ranks.

sentences.zh: 天祐中，幽州劉守光敗，其府掾馮道歸太原，承業辟為本院巡官。

translations.literal: In Tianyou, when Liu Shouguang of Youzhou was defeated, his staff member Feng Dao came to Taiyuan and Chengye took him as patrol officer of the directorate.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianyou, after Youzhou's Liu Shouguang fell, his clerk Feng Dao reached Taiyuan and Chengye made him a directorate patrol officer.

sentences.zh: 承業重其文章履行，甚見待遇。

translations.literal: Chengye valued his literary talent and conduct and treated him very well.
translations.idiomatic: Chengye prized his writing and character and favored him greatly.

sentences.zh: 時有周元豹者，善人倫鑒，與道不合，謂承業曰：「馮生無前程，公不可過用。

translations.literal: There was a Zhou Yuanbao skilled at judging men who disliked Dao and told Chengye, "Master Feng has no future—my lord must not overuse him."
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yuanbao, who read men well, disliked Dao and warned Chengye, "Feng has no prospects ahead—do not lean on him too hard."

sentences.zh: 」管書記盧質聞之曰：「我曾見杜黃裳司空寫真圖，道之狀貌酷類焉，將來必副大用，元豹之言，不足信也。

translations.literal: " Chief secretary Lu Zhi heard this and said, "I once saw the portrait of Minister Du Huangshang; Dao's features are strikingly alike—he will surely rise to great use; Yuanbao's words are not to be trusted."
translations.idiomatic: Chief secretary Lu Zhi said, "I have seen Du Huangshang's portrait—Dao looks just like him and will surely serve at the highest level; do not trust Yuanbao."

sentences.zh: 」承業薦為霸府從事焉。

translations.literal: " Chengye recommended him as staff officer of the hegemon's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Chengye then recommended him as an officer of the hegemon's staff.

sentences.zh: 柏鄉之役，王師既逼汴營，周德威慮其奔衝，堅請退舍。

translations.literal: At the battle of Baixiang the royal army had pressed the Bian camp; Zhou Dewei feared a headlong rush and urgently asked to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: At Baixiang the army had closed on the Bian camp; Zhou Dewei feared a reckless charge and begged to pull back.

sentences.zh: 莊宗怒其懦，不聽，垂帳而寢，諸將不敢言事，鹹詣監軍請白。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong was angry at his timidity and would not listen; he let down the curtain and slept, and the generals dared not speak—all went to the army inspector to report.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong raged at his caution, refused him, drew the curtain, and slept; no general dared speak, and all sought the army inspector.

sentences.zh: 承業遽至牙門，褰帳而入，撫莊宗曰：「此非王安寢時，周德威老將，洞識兵勢，姑務萬全，言不可忽。

translations.literal: Chengye hurried to the headquarters gate, lifted the curtain and entered, and stroking Zhuangzong said, "This is no time for Your Majesty to rest in peace—Zhou Dewei is an old general who knows warfare through and through; for now seek every safeguard; his words must not be ignored."
translations.idiomatic: Chengye rushed to headquarters, swept the curtain aside, and said, "This is no hour for sleep—Dewei is a veteran who reads the field; heed him for safety's sake."

sentences.zh: 」 莊宗蹶然而興曰：「予方思之。

translations.literal: " Zhuangzong started up and said, "I was just thinking of that."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong jolted upright: "I was thinking the same."

sentences.zh: 」其夕，收軍保鄗邑。

translations.literal: " That evening the army withdrew to hold Haoyi.
translations.idiomatic: That night the army fell back to Haoyi.

sentences.zh: 德威討劉守光，令承業往視賊勢，因請莊宗自行，果成大捷。

translations.literal: When Dewei campaigned against Liu Shouguang he sent Chengye to observe the enemy; he also asked Zhuangzong to take the field in person, and a great victory followed.
translations.idiomatic: Dewei sent Chengye to scout Liu Shouguang and urged Zhuangzong to lead in person—the result was a crushing win.

sentences.zh: 承業感武皇厚遇，自莊宗在魏州垂十年，太原軍國政事，一委承業；

translations.literal: Chengye, moved by Wuhuang's great favor, while Zhuangzong was at Weizhou for nearly ten years had all Taiyuan's military and civil affairs entrusted to him alone;
translations.idiomatic: Grateful for Wuhuang's kindness, Chengye for nearly ten years while Zhuangzong was at Weizhou held Taiyuan's army and state in his hands alone;

sentences.zh: 而積聚庾帑，收兵市馬，招懷流散，勸課農桑，成是霸基者，承業之忠力也。

translations.literal: by amassing granaries and treasuries, recruiting soldiers and buying horses, gathering the displaced, and urging farming and mulberry culture, the hegemon's foundation was his loyal strength.
translations.idiomatic: he piled grain and treasure, raised troops and horses, recalled exiles, and urged farming—the hegemon's base was his loyal work.

sentences.zh: 時貞簡太后，韓德妃、伊淑妃、諸宅王之貴，洎王之介弟在晉陽宮，或不以其道幹於承業，悉不聽，逾法禁者必懲，由是貴戚斂手，民俗丕變。

translations.literal: At that time Empress Dowager Zhenjian, Consorts Han and Yi, the noble princes of the various residences, and the king's younger brothers at the Jinyang palace—if any pressed Chengye improperly he would not listen; whoever overstepped the law was punished, so the kinfolk held back and custom greatly changed.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhenjian, the Han and Yi consorts, palace princes, and the king's brothers at Jinyang—none could sway him by improper means; lawbreakers were punished, kinfolk fell silent, and the realm's ways shifted.

sentences.zh: 或有中傷承業於莊宗者，言專弄威柄，廣納賂遺。

translations.literal: Some slandered Chengye to Zhuangzong, saying he monopolized power and took bribes widely.
translations.idiomatic: Some told Zhuangzong he hoarded power and took bribes on every side.

sentences.zh: 莊宗歲時還晉陽宮省太后，須錢蒱博、給伶官，嘗置酒於泉府，莊宗酣飲，命興聖宮使李繼岌為承業起舞，既竟，承業出寶帶幣馬奉之。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong yearly returned to Jinyang to visit the empress dowager he needed money for gambling and actors; once he set wine at the treasury office, drank deep, and ordered Xingsheng Palace envoy Li Jiji to dance for Chengye; when it ended Chengye produced a jeweled belt, coins, and a horse as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Each year Zhuangzong visited the dowager at Jinyang and wanted cash for dice and players; once at the treasury he drank deep and made Li Jiji dance for Chengye, who then gave belt, coin, and horse.

sentences.zh: 莊宗指錢積謂承業曰：「和哥無錢使，七哥與此一積，寶馬非殊惠也。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong pointed at a pile of money and told Chengye, "Brother He has no cash—Seventh Brother, here is a pile for him; the fine horse is no special favor."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong pointed to a heap of coin: "He-ge lacks money—Seventh Brother, take this pile; the horse is nothing special."

sentences.zh: 」承業謝曰：「郎君哥勞，承業自出己俸錢。

translations.literal: " Chengye thanked him and said, "The young lord labored; Chengye pays from his own salary."
translations.idiomatic: Chengye bowed: "The prince has toiled—I pay from my own stipend."

sentences.zh: 此錢是大王庫物，準擬支贍三軍，不敢以公物為私禮也。

translations.literal: This money is the great king's treasury stock, set aside to supply the three armies—I dare not use public goods as a private gift."
translations.idiomatic: That coin is the king's treasury, meant for the three armies—I cannot make a private gift of public wealth."

sentences.zh: 」莊宗不悅，使酒侵承業。

translations.literal: " Zhuangzong was displeased and, drunk, insulted Chengye.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong, displeased and in his cups, insulted him.

sentences.zh: 承業曰：「臣老敕使。

translations.literal: Chengye said, "Your servant is an old imperial messenger."
translations.idiomatic: Chengye said, "I am an old palace envoy."

sentences.zh: 非為子孫之謀，惜錢為大王基業，王若自要散施，何妨老夫，不過財盡兵散，一事無成。」

translations.literal: It is not for my descendants' sake that I spare the money for the great king's foundation; if Your Majesty insists on scattering it, what harm to this old man—only that wealth will be spent, the army dispersed, and nothing achieved."
translations.idiomatic: I do not hoard coin for my heirs but for your foundation; scatter it if you will—wealth will fail, the army scatter, and all be lost."

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note:

sentences.zh: （案：《通鑒》作王自取用之，何問仆為！）〉

translations.literal: (Note: The 《Comprehensive Mirror》 reads: "If the king takes it for himself, why ask the servant!")〉
translations.idiomatic: (Per the 《Comprehensive Mirror》: "If Your Majesty takes it yourself, why ask a servant!")〉

sentences.zh: 莊宗怒，顧元行欽曰：「取劍來！

translations.literal: Zhuangzong was furious and turned to Yuan Xingqin: "Bring a sword!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong raged and called to Yuan Xingqin, "Fetch a sword!"

sentences.zh: 」承業引莊宗衣，泣而言曰：「仆荷先王遺顧，誓為本朝誅汴賊，為王惜庫物，斬承業首，死亦無愧於先王，今日請死！

translations.literal: " Chengye seized Zhuangzong's robe and weeping said, "Your servant bears the late king's dying charge, sworn to destroy the Bian rebels for this dynasty and to spare the treasury for the king—cut off Chengye's head and I die without shame to the late king; today I ask to die!"
translations.idiomatic: Chengye clutched his robe and wept: "I owe the late king's trust, vowed to kill the Bian rebels and guard the treasury—take my head and I die clean; I ask for death today!"

sentences.zh: 」閻寶解承業手，令退。

translations.literal: " Yan Bao released Chengye's hand and had him withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Bao freed his hand and sent him out.

sentences.zh: 承業詬寶曰：「黨朱溫逆賊，未嘗有一言效忠，而敢依阿諂附。

translations.literal: Chengye reviled Bao: "You sided with the traitor Zhu Wen and never once spoke loyalty, yet dare fawn and cling."
translations.idiomatic: Chengye cursed him: "You clung to Zhu Wen the rebel and never spoke loyalty, yet dare to flatter."

sentences.zh: 」揮拳踣之。

translations.literal: " He swung his fist and knocked him down.
translations.idiomatic: He struck him down with his fist.

sentences.zh: 太后聞莊宗酒失，急召入。

translations.literal: The empress dowager heard of Zhuangzong's drunken lapse and urgently summoned him in.
translations.idiomatic: The dowager heard of the drunken scene and summoned Zhuangzong at once.

sentences.zh: 莊宗性至孝，聞太后召，叩頭謝阿業曰：「吾杯酒之間，忤於七哥，太后必怪吾。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong was deeply filial; hearing the dowager's summons he kowtowed to Chengye and said, "Between cups I offended Seventh Brother—the dowager is sure to blame me."
translations.idiomatic: Filial to the core, Zhuangzong kowtowed: "I offended Seventh Brother over wine—the dowager will blame me."

sentences.zh: 七哥為痛飲兩卮分謗，可乎？

translations.literal: Will Seventh Brother drink two cups with me to share the blame—may he?"
translations.idiomatic: Will Seventh Brother drink two cups and share the blame?"

sentences.zh: 」莊宗連飲四鍾，勸承業，竟不飲。

translations.literal: " Zhuangzong drank four goblets in a row and urged Chengye, who would not drink at all.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong drained four cups and pressed Chengye, who refused every one.

sentences.zh: 莊宗歸宮，太后使人謂承業曰：「小兒忤特進，已笞矣，可歸第。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong returned to the palace; the dowager sent word to Chengye: "The boy offended the special commissioner and has been beaten—return home."
translations.idiomatic: Back at the palace the dowager sent word: "The boy offended you and has been flogged—go home."

sentences.zh: 」翌日，太后與莊宗俱幸其第，慰勞之。

translations.literal: " The next day the dowager and Zhuangzong together visited his residence to comfort him.
translations.idiomatic: Next day dowager and son visited his house to console him.

sentences.zh: 自是私謁幾絕。

translations.literal: From then on private visits nearly ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Private visits thereafter nearly stopped.

sentences.zh: 十四年，承製授開府儀同三司、左衛上將軍、燕國公，固辭不受。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year an imperial writ appointed him Grand Mentor of the State, Left Guard Senior General, and Duke of Yan; he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: In year fourteen he was offered Grand Mentor, Left Guard Senior General, and Duke of Yan by imperial writ and refused.

sentences.zh: 是時，盧質在莊宗幕下，嗜酒輕傲，嘗呼莊宗諸弟為豚犬，莊宗深銜之。

translations.literal: At that time Lu Zhi was on Zhuangzong's staff, fond of wine and arrogant; he once called Zhuangzong's younger brothers pigs and dogs, and Zhuangzong deeply resented it.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi on Zhuangzong's staff drank hard and sneered, once calling the princes swine and dogs—Zhuangzong hated him for it.

sentences.zh: 承業慮質被禍，因乘間謂莊宗曰：「盧質多行無禮，臣請為大王殺之，可乎？

translations.literal: Chengye feared Zhi would come to harm and seized a moment to tell Zhuangzong, "Lu Zhi acts without propriety again and again—your servant asks to kill him for the great king—may I?"
translations.idiomatic: Fearing for Zhi, Chengye said, "Lu Zhi is insolent again—shall I kill him for you?"

sentences.zh: 」莊宗曰：「予方招禮賢士，以開霸業，七哥何言之過也！

translations.literal: " Zhuangzong said, "I am just now recruiting worthy men to open the hegemony—how can Seventh Brother speak so harshly!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong said, "I am gathering talent to build the realm—how can you speak so, Seventh Brother!"

sentences.zh: 」 承業因聳立而言曰：「大王若能如此，何憂不得天下！

translations.literal: " Chengye then stood erect and said, "If the great king can be like this, what worry is there of not winning the realm!"
translations.idiomatic: Chengye stood tall: "If you can be thus, what realm will you not win!"

sentences.zh: 」其後盧質雖成縱誕，莊宗終能容之，蓋承業為之藻藉也。

translations.literal: " Thereafter though Lu Zhi grew ever more unrestrained, Zhuangzong could still tolerate him—largely because Chengye gave him cover.
translations.idiomatic: Though Zhi grew wilder, Zhuangzong bore with him—Chengye had smoothed the way.

sentences.zh: 十八年，莊宗受諸道勸進，將纂帝位。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Zhuangzong received urging from the circuits and was about to seize the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In year eighteen the circuits pressed Zhuangzong to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 承業以為晉王三代有功於國，先人怒朱氏弑逆，將復舊邦，讎既未平，不宜輕受推戴。

translations.literal: Chengye held that the Prince of Jin's house for three generations had served the state with merit, that the forebears raged at the Zhu clan's regicide and meant to restore the old realm—the foe was not yet subdued and he should not lightly accept elevation.
translations.idiomatic: Chengye argued that three Jin generations had served Tang, that they fought to avenge regicide and restore Tang—the enemy remained and elevation was premature.

sentences.zh: 方疾作，肩輿之鄴宮，見莊宗曰：「王父子血戰三十餘年，蓋言報國仇讎，復唐宗社。

translations.literal: Though ill, he was carried in a litter to the Ye palace and told Zhuangzong, "Father and son have fought bloodily for more than thirty years—was it not to avenge the state and restore Tang's altars?"
translations.idiomatic: Ill, he was carried to Ye and said, "Thirty years of bloodshed—was it not to avenge Tang and restore its altars?"

sentences.zh: 今元凶未滅，民賦已殫，而遽先大號，蠹耗財力，臣以為不可一也。

translations.literal: The chief culprit is not yet destroyed, the people's levies are exhausted, yet you hasten to take the great title—it will waste strength; your servant holds that this is impermissible—the first point."
translations.idiomatic: The arch-enemy lives, taxes are spent—yet you seize the imperial name and drain strength; that is my first objection."

sentences.zh: 臣自咸通已來，伏事宮掖，每見國家冊命大禮，儀仗法物，百司庶務，經年草定，臨事猶有不可。

translations.literal: Your servant since Xiantong has served the inner palace and each time has seen the state's enthronement rites, regalia, and the hundred offices' affairs take years to draft—yet at the event things still go wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Since Xiantong I have watched enthronements: regalia and offices need years of planning, and still things fail at the last.

sentences.zh: 王若化家為國，新立廟朝，不可乖於制度。

translations.literal: If the king turns his house into a state and raises a new temple court, he must not depart from the institutions.
translations.idiomatic: Turn house into realm and you must not break ritual law—that is my second point.

sentences.zh: 制禮作樂，未見其人，臣以為不可二也。

translations.literal: To fix rites and make music—no fit man is in sight; your servant holds that this is impermissible—the second point."
translations.idiomatic: Rites and music want a master none has found—that is my second objection."

sentences.zh: 舉事量力而行，不可信於遊譚也。」

translations.literal: Undertake affairs according to capacity; do not trust idle talk."
translations.idiomatic: Measure deeds to strength; do not trust loose talk."

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note:

sentences.zh: （《通鑒考異》引秦再思《洛中記異》云：承業諫帝曰：「大王何不待誅克梁孽，更平吳、蜀，俾天下一家，且先求唐氏子孫立之，後更以天下讓有功者，何人輒敢當之！

translations.literal: (The 《Zizhi tongjian kaoyi》 cites Qin Zaishi's 《Luozhong jiyi》: Chengye admonished the emperor, "Why does the great king not wait until the Liang scourge is destroyed and Wu and Shu pacified, so the realm is one family—first seek a Tang descendant to set up, then yield the realm to the meritorious—who would dare take it!"
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Zizhi tongjian: Textual Variants》 cites Qin Zaishi's 《Strange Records of Luoyang》: Chengye said, "Why not destroy Liang, pacify Wu and Shu, find a Tang heir, then yield the realm to merit—who would dare claim it!"

sentences.zh: 讓一月即一月牢，讓一年即一年牢。

translations.literal: Yield for a month and it is a month's prison; yield for a year and it is a year's prison.
translations.idiomatic: A month of yielding is a month's cage; a year's yielding, a year's cage.

sentences.zh: 設使高祖再生，太宗復出，又胡為哉！

translations.literal: Suppose Gaozu were reborn and Taizong returned—what then!
translations.idiomatic: If Gaozu lived again and Taizong returned—what then!

sentences.zh: 今大王一旦自立，頓失從前仗義征伐之旨，人情怠矣。

translations.literal: Now the great king sets himself up at once and at once loses the righteous purpose of the campaigns of old—the people's hearts grow slack.
translations.idiomatic: Proclaim yourself now and you lose the righteous war you waged—hearts will slacken.

sentences.zh: 老夫是閹官，不愛大王官職富貴，直以受先王付屬之重，欲為大王立萬年之基爾。」）〉

translations.literal: This old man is a eunuch; I do not love rank and riches for the great king—I only bear the late king's heavy charge and wish to lay a foundation of ten thousand years for the great king.")〉
translations.idiomatic: I am a eunuch, not greedy for your honors—I owe the late king's trust and seek your lasting foundation.")〉

sentences.zh: 莊宗曰：「奈諸將何？

translations.literal: Zhuangzong said, "What of the generals?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong said, "But the generals?"

sentences.zh: 」承業知莊宗不從，因號泣而言之。

translations.literal: " Knowing Zhuangzong would not heed him, Chengye wept as he spoke.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing refusal, Chengye wept as he spoke.

sentences.zh: 十九年十一月二日，以疾卒於晉陽之第，時年七十七。

translations.literal: On the second day of the eleventh month of the nineteenth year he died of illness at his Taiyuan residence, aged seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: On 19.11.2 he died at his Taiyuan house, aged seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 貞簡太后聞喪，遽至其第盡哀，為之行服，如兒侄禮。

translations.literal: Hearing of the death, Empress Dowager Zhenjian hurried to his house and mourned fully, wearing mourning for him as for a son or nephew.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhenjian rushed to mourn him in full mourning, as for kin.

sentences.zh: 同光初，贈左武衛上將軍，諡曰貞憲。

translations.literal: At the start of Tongguang he was posthumously made Left Martial Guard Senior General with the posthumous name Zhenxian.
translations.idiomatic: In early Tongguang he was posthumously Left Martial Guard Senior General, posthumous name Zhenxian.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note:

sentences.zh: （《五代史闕文》：莊宗將即位於魏州，承業自太原至，謂莊宗曰：「吾王世奉唐家，最為忠孝，自貞觀以來，王室有難，未嘗不從。

translations.literal: (《Wudai shi quewen》: As Zhuangzong was about to ascend at Weizhou, Chengye came from Taiyuan and told Zhuangzong, "Our house for generations has served Tang most loyally; since Zhenguan, whenever the royal house was in peril we never failed to answer.
translations.idiomatic: (《Lost Passages of the History of the Five Dynasties》: As Zhuangzong was to ascend at Weizhou, Chengye came from Taiyuan and said, "Our line has served Tang loyally since Zhenguan and never failed the throne in crisis."

sentences.zh: 所以老奴三十餘年為吾王捃拾財賦、召補軍馬者，誓滅逆賊朱溫，復本朝宗社耳。

translations.literal: For more than thirty years this old servant has gathered wealth and recruited soldiers for our king, sworn to destroy the rebel Zhu Wen and restore the dynasty's altars.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty years I gathered wealth and troops to destroy Zhu Wen and restore Tang.

sentences.zh: 今河朔甫定，朱氏尚存，吾王遽即大位，可乎？

translations.literal: Now the Hebei is just settled and Zhu still lives—may our king at once take the great title?"
translations.idiomatic: Hebei is barely settled and Zhu Wen still lives—will you take the throne now?"

sentences.zh: 」云云。

translations.literal: And so on.
translations.idiomatic: And so on.

sentences.zh: 莊宗曰：「奈諸將意何！

translations.literal: Zhuangzong said, "What of the generals' minds!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong said, "What of the generals' will!"

sentences.zh: 」承業知不可諫止，乃慟哭曰：「諸侯血戰者，本為李家，今吾王自取之，誤老奴矣！

translations.literal: " Chengye knew he could not dissuade him and wailed, "The lords fought in blood for the Li house—now our king takes it for himself and has wronged this old servant!"
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he could not prevail, Chengye wailed, "They bled for the Lis—now you seize the throne yourself and wrong me!"

sentences.zh: 」即歸太原，不食而死。

translations.literal: " He returned to Taiyuan and starved himself to death.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to Taiyuan and starved himself dead.

sentences.zh: 臣謹按：《莊宗實錄》敘承業諫即位事甚詳，惟「吾王自取」之言不書，史官諱之也。）〉

translations.literal: Your servant notes: The 《Zhuangzong shilu》 narrates Chengye's remonstrance on enthronement in detail, but does not record the words "our king takes it for himself"—the historians avoided them.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Veritable Records of Zhuangzong》 tells the remonstrance fully but omits "our king takes it himself"—the scribes shied from it.

sentences.zh: 張居翰，字德卿。

translations.literal: Zhang Juhan, styled Deqing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Juhan, styled Deqing.

sentences.zh: 咸通初，掖庭令張從玫養之為子，以蔭入仕。

translations.literal: Early in Xiantong, Palace Director Zhang Congmei raised him as a son; he entered office by hereditary privilege.
translations.idiomatic: Early Xiantong, Zhang Congmei adopted him; he entered office by privilege.

sentences.zh: 中和三年，自容管監軍判官入為學士院判官，遷樞密承旨、內府令，賜緋。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhonghe he came from Rongguan army inspector and secretariat judge to Hanlin Academy judge, rose to Bureau of Military Affairs commissioner and inner palace director, and was granted crimson.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonghe 3 he came from Rongguan as inspector-secretary judge to Hanlin judge, then Bureau commissioner and inner director with crimson robes.

sentences.zh: 昭宗在華下，超授內常侍，出監幽州軍事，秩滿詔歸，節度使劉仁恭表留之。

translations.literal: While Zhaozong was west of the mountains he was abruptly made Inner Attendant and sent out to oversee Youzhou; when his term ended an edict recalled him, but Military Commissioner Liu Rengong memorialized to keep him.
translations.idiomatic: At Huashan Zhaozong made him Inner Attendant and sent him to Youzhou; recalled at term's end, Liu Rengong asked to keep him.

sentences.zh: 天復中，詔誅宦官，仁恭紿奏殺之，匿於大安山之北溪。

translations.literal: In Tianfu the court ordered eunuchs killed; Rengong falsely reported he had killed him and hid him in a north ravine of Mount Da'an.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianfu eunuchs were ordered killed; Rengong claimed the deed and hid him in Da'an's northern ravine.

sentences.zh: 天祐三年，汴人攻滄州，仁恭求援於武皇，乃遣居翰與書記馬鬱等率兵助武皇同攻潞州，武皇因留之不遣。

translations.literal: In Tianyou 3 the Bian army attacked Cangzhou; Rengong sought aid from Wuhuang and sent Juhan with secretary Ma Yu and others to lead troops aiding Wuhuang's attack on Luzhou; Wuhuang kept him and would not release him.
translations.idiomatic: Tianyou 3 Bian attacked Cangzhou; Rengong asked Wuhuang for aid and sent Juhan and Ma Yu to help attack Luzhou—Wuhuang detained him.

sentences.zh: 李嗣昭節制昭義，以居翰監其軍，以燕軍三千為部下。

translations.literal: Li Sizhao governed Zhaoyi and made Juhan oversee his army with three thousand Yan troops as his command.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sizhao of Zhaoyi put Juhan over the army with three thousand Yan troops.

sentences.zh: 俄而汴將李思安築夾城以圍潞州，居翰與嗣昭登城保守，以至解圍。

translations.literal: Soon Bian general Li Si'an built Jiacheng to besiege Luzhou; Juhan and Sizhao held the walls until relief broke the siege.
translations.idiomatic: Li Si'an walled Jiacheng around Luzhou; Juhan and Sizhao held the city until relief came.

sentences.zh: 自是嗣昭每出征，令居翰知留後事。

translations.literal: Thereafter whenever Sizhao marched out he left Juhan to manage rear affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After that Sizhao left rear affairs to Juhan whenever he campaigned.

sentences.zh: 同光元年夏四月，召為樞密使，加特進，與郭崇韜對掌機務。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer, Tongguang 1, he was summoned as Bureau commissioner, given special advancement, and with Guo Chongtao jointly held the secrets of state.
translations.idiomatic: Tongguang 1.4 he became Bureau commissioner with special advancement and shared state secrets with Guo Chongtao.

sentences.zh: 十月，莊宗將渡河，留居翰與李紹宏同守魏州。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, as Zhuangzong was about to cross the Yellow River, he left Juhan and Li Shaohong together to guard Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Zhuangzong prepared to cross the river and left Juhan and Li Shaohong to hold Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 莊宗入汴，加驃騎大將軍，知內侍省事，依前充樞密使。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong entered Bian he was made Grand General of the Agile Cavalry, put in charge of inner palace affairs, and continued as Bureau commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Entering Bian, he became Grand General of the Agile Cavalry, directed inner palace affairs, and kept his Bureau post.

sentences.zh: 同光時，宦官幹政，邦家之務皆出於郭崇韜。

translations.literal: In the Tongguang era eunuchs meddled in government; the state's affairs all issued from Guo Chongtao.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tongguang the eunuchs ruled; state business flowed from Guo Chongtao.

sentences.zh: 居翰自以羈旅乘時，擢居重地，每於宣授，不敢有所是非，承顏免過而已，以此脫季年之禍。

translations.literal: Juhan, seeing himself a wanderer who had risen in troubled times to a weighty post, at every appointment announcement dared not judge right or wrong and only matched his expression to avoid fault—by this he escaped disaster in his later years.
translations.idiomatic: A stranger lifted by the times, Juhan at each posting dared not judge and only smiled along—thus he survived his last years.

sentences.zh: 四年三月，偽蜀王衍既降，詔遷其族於洛陽。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourth year, after the false Shu king Wang Yan had surrendered, an edict moved his clan to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In month three of year four, after the Shu pretender Wang Yan surrendered, the court ordered his clan moved to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 行及秦川，時關東已亂，莊宗慮衍為變，遣中官向延嗣馳騎齎詔殺之。

translations.literal: When they reached Qinchuan the east of the passes was already in turmoil; Zhuangzong feared Yan might rebel and sent palace envoy Xiang Yansi riding hard with an edict to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: At Qinchuan the east was in chaos; fearing revolt, Zhuangzong sent Xiang Yansi with an edict to kill him.

sentences.zh: 詔云：「王衍一行，並宜殺戮。

translations.literal: The edict read: "Wang Yan's entire party should be put to death."
translations.idiomatic: The edict said, "Wang Yan's whole train shall be executed."

sentences.zh: 」其詔已經印畫，時居翰在密地，覆視其詔，即就殿柱揩云「行」字，改書「家」字。

translations.literal: " The edict had already been sealed; Juhan was in a private room reviewing it and at once on a hall pillar erased the character for "party" and wrote the character for "family" instead.
translations.idiomatic: The seal was already set; Juhan in a side room saw the edict, scraped the character "party" on a pillar post, and wrote "family" in its place.

sentences.zh: 及衍就戮於秦川驛，止族其近屬而已，其偽官及從行者尚千餘人，皆免其枉濫，居翰之力也。

translations.literal: When Yan was executed at Qinchuan post station only his close kin were killed; more than a thousand false officials and followers were spared wrongful slaughter—Juhan's doing.
translations.idiomatic: At Qinchuan station only Yan's near kin died; a thousand pseudo-officials and followers were spared—Juhan's deed.

sentences.zh: 明宗入洛，居翰謁見於至德宮，待罪雪涕，乞歸田里，詔許之，乃辭歸長安。

translations.literal: When Mingzong entered Luoyang, Juhan presented himself at Zhide Palace, confessed fault with tears, and begged to return to his fields; an edict allowed it and he took leave for Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong entering Luoyang, Juhan met him at Zhide Palace, wept his confession, and begged retirement; the edict granted it and he went home to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 仍以其子延貴為西京職事，以供侍養。

translations.literal: His son Yanzhen was still made western capital duty officer to support his upkeep.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yanzhen was made western capital duty officer to provide for him.

sentences.zh: 天成三年四月，以疾卒於長安，時年七十一。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of Tiancheng 3 he died of illness at Chang'an, aged seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: Tiancheng 3.4 he died at Chang'an of illness, aged seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 居翰性和而靜，諳悉舊事。

translations.literal: Juhan's nature was gentle and quiet, and he was well versed in old precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Gentle and quiet by nature, he knew the old precedents well.

sentences.zh: 在潞州累年，每春課人育蔬種樹，敦本惠農，有仁者之心焉。

translations.literal: During his many years at Luzhou each spring he set people to raise vegetables and plant trees, urging the root and favoring farmers—he had a humane heart.
translations.idiomatic: At Luzhou for years he each spring had people plant vegetables and trees, cherishing the root and helping farmers—a humane man.

sentences.zh: 馬紹宏，閹官也。

translations.literal: Ma Shaohong was a eunuch.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shaohong was a palace eunuch.

sentences.zh: 初與孟知祥同為中門使，及周德威薨，莊宗兼領幽州，令紹宏權知州事。

translations.literal: At first he and Meng Zhixiang were both middle-gate envoys; when Zhou Dewei died Zhuangzong also took Youzhou and made Shaohong acting prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He and Meng Zhixiang had been middle-gate envoys; when Dewei died Zhuangzong took Youzhou and left Shaohong as acting prefect.

sentences.zh: 即位之初，郭崇韜勳望高，舊在紹宏之下，時征潞州監軍張居翰與崇韜並為樞密使，紹宏失望，乃以為宣徽使。

translations.literal: At the start of enthronement Guo Chongtao's merit stood high though he had once ranked below Shaohong; when Luzhou army inspector Zhang Juhan was summoned with Chongtao as Bureau commissioners, Shaohong was disappointed and was made Xuanhui commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the reign Chongtao's fame outshone him though he had once outranked Chongtao; Juhan and Chongtao became Bureau commissioners and Shaohong, disappointed, was made Xuanhui commissioner.

sentences.zh: 紹宏以己合當樞密任，常鬱鬱側目於崇韜。

translations.literal: Shaohong held that he ought to have had the Bureau post and constantly glared sidelong at Chongtao.
translations.idiomatic: He believed the Bureau seat was his and eyed Chongtao with constant resentment.

sentences.zh: 崇韜知其慊也，乃置內勾之目，令天下錢穀薄書，悉委裁遣。

translations.literal: Chongtao knew his grievance and therefore created the post of inner auditor, putting all the realm's revenue ledgers under his disposal.
translations.idiomatic: Chongtao knew his spite and invented the inner-auditor post, handing him every province's accounts.

sentences.zh: 既而州郡供報，輒滋煩費，議者以為十羊九牧，深所不可，內勾之目，人以為是妖言。

translations.literal: Soon the circuits' reports grew ever more burdensome; critics said it was ten shepherds for nine sheep and deeply wrong—the inner-auditor title people took for an evil omen.
translations.idiomatic: Reports from the circuits grew costly; critics called it ten shepherds for nine sheep—a post people took for an ill omen.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note:

sentences.zh: （案：下有闕文。

translations.literal: (Note: Text is missing below.
translations.idiomatic: (Text missing below.

sentences.zh: 據《通鑒》，李嗣源為謠言所屬，危殆者數四，賴宣徽使李紹宏左右營護，以是得全。

translations.literal: According to the Comprehensive Mirror, Li Siyuan was several times brought to the brink by slanderous talk and only because Xuanhui Commissioner Li Shaohong guarded him on every side did he survive.
translations.idiomatic: Per the Comprehensive Mirror, Li Siyuan was nearly destroyed four times by rumor and was saved only by Xuanhui Commissioner Li Shaohong's constant protection.

sentences.zh: 天成元年二月己丑朔，以宣徽南院使李紹宏為樞密使。）〉

translations.literal: On the first day of the second month of Tiancheng 1, Southern Xuanhui Commissioner Li Shaohong was made Bureau commissioner.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Tiancheng 1.2.1 Li Shaohong of the southern Xuanhui office became Bureau commissioner.)〉

sentences.zh: 孟漢瓊，本鎮州王鎔之小豎也。

translations.literal: Meng Hanqiong was originally a young attendant of Wang Rong of Zhen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Hanqiong had begun as a boy attendant to Zhenzhou's Wang Rong.

sentences.zh: 明宗鎮常山，得侍左右。

translations.literal: When Mingzong held Changshan he came to serve at his side.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong governed Changshan Hanqiong waited on him.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，自諸司使累遷宣徽南院使。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne he rose from various office commissioners to Southern Xuanhui commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On Mingzong's accession he climbed from bureau posts to Southern Xuanhui commissioner.

sentences.zh: 漢瓊性通黠，善交構。

translations.literal: Hanqiong was clever and sly and skilled at intrigue.
translations.idiomatic: Clever, sharp, and skilled in intrigue.

sentences.zh: 初見秦王權重，及挾王淑妃勢，傾心事之；

translations.literal: At first he saw the Prince of Qin's power and, leaning on Consort Wang Shufei's influence, threw himself into serving him;
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the Prince of Qin's weight and Consort Wang Shufei's power, he devoted himself to the prince;

sentences.zh: 及朱、馮用事，又與之締結。

translations.literal: when Zhu and Feng held sway he bonded with them as well.
translations.idiomatic: when Zhu and Feng ruled he allied with them too.

sentences.zh: 秦王領兵至天津橋，時漢瓊與朱、馮及康義誠方會議於內庭，謀猶未決，漢瓊獨出死力，先入殿門，奏於明宗，語在《秦王傳》。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Qin led troops to Tianjin Bridge, Hanqiong with Zhu, Feng, and Kang Yicheng were meeting in the inner court and the plan was still unsettled; Hanqiong alone exerted himself to the death, entered the palace gate first, and reported to Mingzong—the account is in the biography of the Prince of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: The prince marched to Tianjin Bridge while Hanqiong, Zhu, Feng, and Kang Yicheng debated in the inner court; Hanqiong alone rushed in first to report to Mingzong, as told in the Prince of Qin's biography.

sentences.zh: 漢瓊即自介馬以召禁軍。

translations.literal: Hanqiong at once took the relay horse to summon the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: He seized a relay horse and called out the guard.

sentences.zh: 秦王既誅，翌日，令漢瓊馳騎召閔帝於鄴。

translations.literal: After the Prince of Qin was executed, the next day Hanqiong was ordered to ride hard and summon the Min Emperor from Ye.
translations.idiomatic: The prince dead, next day Hanqiong was sent to fetch the Min Emperor from Ye.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note:

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》：遣漢瓊征從厚，且權知天雄軍府事。）〉

translations.literal: (The Comprehensive Mirror: He sent Hanqiong to campaign against Conghou and also made him acting prefect of Tianxiong headquarters.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Comprehensive Mirror: Hanqiong was sent against Conghou and made acting prefect of Tianxiong.)〉

sentences.zh: 閔帝嗣位，尤恃恩寵，期月之內，累加開府儀同三司、驃騎大將軍。

translations.literal: When the Min Emperor succeeded he especially relied on Hanqiong's favor; within a month he was repeatedly promoted to Grand Mentor of the State and Grand General of the Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Conghou on succeeding leaned on Hanqiong and within a month piled on Grand Mentor and Grand General of the Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 西軍既叛，閔帝急召漢瓊，欲令先入於鄴，漢瓊藏匿不行。

translations.literal: When the western army rebelled the Min Emperor urgently summoned Hanqiong, wishing him to enter Ye first; Hanqiong hid and would not go.
translations.idiomatic: The western army rose; Conghou called Hanqiong to enter Ye ahead of him, but Hanqiong hid and refused.

sentences.zh: 潞王行及陝州，乃悉召諸妓妾訣別，欲手刃之，眾知其心，率皆藏竄。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Lu reached Shaan Prefecture Hanqiong gathered all his singing girls and concubines to bid farewell and meant to kill them with his own hand; the crowd knew his mind and mostly hid away.
translations.idiomatic: At Shaanzhou the Prince of Lu approaching, Hanqiong called his women to farewell and meant to kill them; knowing his intent, they hid.

sentences.zh: 初，潞王失守於河中，勒歸於清化裏第。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Prince of Lu lost his post at Hezhong he was compelled back to his residence on Qinghua Lane.
translations.idiomatic: Once, when the prince lost Hezhong he was forced back to Qinghua Lane.

sentences.zh: 時王淑妃恒令漢瓊傳教旨於潞王，王善待之，故漢瓊自謂潞王於己有恩。

translations.literal: Consort Wang Shufei often had Hanqiong convey edicts to the Prince of Lu, and the prince treated him well, so Hanqiong believed the prince owed him kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Wang Shufei had Hanqiong carry messages to the prince, who favored him—Hanqiong thought the prince was in his debt.

sentences.zh: 至是，乃單騎至澠池謁見潞王，因自慟哭，欲有所陳。

translations.literal: Now he came alone on horseback to Mianchi to meet the Prince of Lu and wept of himself, wishing to speak.
translations.idiomatic: He rode alone to Mianchi, met the prince, and wept, wanting to speak.

sentences.zh: 潞王曰：「 諸事不言可知。

translations.literal: The Prince of Lu said, "All matters need not be spoken to be known."
translations.idiomatic: The prince said, "Everything is clear without words."

sentences.zh: 」漢瓊即自預從臣之列，尋戮於路左。

translations.literal: " Hanqiong at once counted himself among the followers and was soon executed by the roadside.
translations.idiomatic: Hanqiong joined the train of followers and was soon killed by the road.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：承業感武皇之大惠，佐莊宗之中興，既義且忠，何以階也。

translations.literal: The historian says: Chengye, moved by Wuhuang's great favor, aided Zhuangzong's restoration—both righteous and loyal; how could he be ranked with them?
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Chengye, grateful for Wuhuang's grace, helped Zhuangzong restore the realm—loyal and just; how compare him to others?

sentences.zh: 夫如是，則晉之勃貂，秦之景監，去之遠矣。

translations.literal: If so, then Jin's Bo Diao and Qin's Jing Jian stand far removed.
translations.idiomatic: Then Bo Diao of Jin and Jing Jian of Qin are worlds apart.

sentences.zh: 居翰改一字於詔書，救千人之濫死，可不謂之仁人矣乎！

translations.literal: Juhan changed one character in an edict and saved a thousand from indiscriminate death—may he not be called a humane man!
translations.idiomatic: Juhan altered one word in an edict and spared a thousand wrongful deaths—is he not humane?

sentences.zh: 如紹宏之爭權，漢瓊之構禍，乃宦者之常態也，又何足以道哉！

translations.literal: As for Shaohong's struggle for power and Hanqiong's sowing of disaster, these are the eunuchs' usual ways—what is there worth speaking of!
translations.idiomatic: Shaohong's grasping and Hanqiong's plotting are eunuchs' common ways—why mention them at all!
